Run a Virtual Conference Using Only Open Source Tools

opensource.com · 3 Oct 2026

A guide on opensource.com walks organizers through hosting a full virtual conference with open-source software only

Covers Jitsi for video, Mattermost for chat, and Nextcloud for file sharing. All tools self-hostable. Estimated server cost: 500-2,000 TRY/month on a Turkish VPS. No proprietary SaaS required. Suitable for 50-500 attendees.

  • Guide published on opensource.com, October 1, 2026.
  • Uses Jitsi for video, Mattermost for chat, Nextcloud for files.
  • All tools are self-hostable.
  • Estimated server cost: 500-2,000 TRY/month on Turkish VPS.
  • Suitable for 50-500 attendees per the guide.

Why it matters

opensource.com outlines hosting a full virtual conference using only open-source software. This removes licensing fees, though the guide is unverified and requires technical skill.

Aleph Alpha Releases Kolibri, Germany's First Sovereign Open-Weight AI Model

tej.as · 3 Oct 2026

Aleph Alpha shipped Kolibri, an open-weight LLM trained on German data, giving EU organizations a self-hostable alternative to US cloud models

The 7B-parameter model is available under a permissive license. Aleph Alpha is a Heidelberg-based company. Kolibri supports German, English, French, and Spanish. The model can run on a single GPU with 24 GB VRAM. Organizations in Türkiye can fine-tune it on Turkish data without sending data abroad.

  • Aleph Alpha released Kolibri, a 7B-parameter open-weight model on October 2, 2026.
  • Model supports German, English, French, and Spanish out of the box.
  • Runs on a single GPU with 24 GB VRAM per the vendor.
  • Licensed permissively for commercial and self-hosted use.
  • Trained primarily on German-language and EU-sourced data.

Why it matters

Partially verified report says Aleph Alpha shipped Kolibri, an open-weight LLM trained on German data. EU organizations can self-host it, reducing reliance on US cloud models.

Cloudflare Launches OHTTP Gateway for Oblivious HTTP

blog.cloudflare.com · 3 Oct 2026

Cloudflare published an OHTTP gateway, enabling privacy-preserving proxy relays that hide client IPs from upstream servers

OHTTP is an IETF standard (draft-ietf-ohai-ohttp). Cloudflare's gateway is open-source. Useful for journalists, activists, and operators who need to mask traffic origin. Supports JSON and binary payloads. Latency overhead is ~50ms per the blog.

  • Cloudflare announced OHTTP gateway on October 2, 2026.
  • OHTTP is an IETF standard (draft-ietf-ohai-ohttp).
  • Gateway code is open-source.
  • Latency overhead approximately 50ms per Cloudflare.
  • Supports JSON and binary payloads.

Why it matters

Verified Cloudflare announcement launches an OHTTP gateway hiding client IPs from upstream servers. This strengthens privacy for users and sites routing through the relay.

Read through the lens · Analysis & Opinion
Web infrastructure is standardizing privacy-preserving proxy layers to reduce tracking

Kagi Orion Search Expands to Linux and Windows

blog.kagi.com · 3 Oct 2026

Kagi's AI-powered search client Orion is now available on Linux and Windows, not just macOS

Orion is a local search front-end that queries Kagi's index. The Linux and Windows beta launched this week. Kagi costs $5/month for 100 searches. A self-hosted instance is not offered. Useful as a Google-alternative desktop search for English-language docs.

  • Kagi released Orion for Linux and Windows on October 3, 2026.
  • Orion previously available on macOS only.
  • Kagi pricing: $5/month for 100 searches.
  • No self-hosted option offered by Kagi.
  • AI-powered local search front-end querying Kagi index.

Why it matters

Reported update says Kagi's Orion search client now runs on Linux and Windows, not just macOS. This gives non-Apple users access to its paid, ad-free search.

Colophon & Method

Lens & Facts — how this paper chooses and frames

Selection, questions and framing are governed by an energy-literate scientific materialism and a dialectical method — facts are not. Every factual claim carries a source; the lens never alters a number, date or quote; a claim that contradicts the lens is reported, not suppressed. Settled evidence is called settled with citations; genuinely contested positions both appear with their evidence. News summaries, analysis and opinion are visually distinct, and analysis always reads through the lens. The machine audits itself in public: errors are corrected openly, and periodic "stories that broke our frame" exercises use the lens's own tools to test its default narrative. Funding, cost and conflicts are disclosed here, in the State of the Machine.

Coverage spans the region and the world. Opportunities are judged by a simple test: can a working person actually act on this, and does it improve their real conditions or their community's? Anything that gates its benefit behind money, status or existing wealth is excluded. Verification: no claim is marked fully verified without independent sources; verdicts are a prompt to read critically, not a substitute for it.
